title: Micro-block coalescer and staged host residency for blocked KV caching
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a micro-block coalescing layer and staged host-residency policy for our blocked/paged KV cache to reduce GPU OOM events and tail latency during continuous batching workloads. This ticket captures the detailed design, heuristics, implementation tasks, and rollout plan for a solution that admits smaller 'micro-block' allocations and coalesces them into resident blocks on the GPU while allowing controlled host staging for cold or low-affinity keys.
background: Current blocked KV allocator favors large fixed-size blocks which reduces fragmentation but increases peak GPU memory pressure for workloads with many short-lived contexts and skewed token affinity. Under sustained continuous batching the runtime triggers aggressive GPU-to-host swapping, causing tail latency spikes and occasional OOM-triggered fallbacks. Existing artifacts (simulator traces and production flamegraphs) show repeated high-frequency swaps for blocks that would be better served via micro-coalescing and soft host residency.
proposal: Introduce a two-tier block strategy: micro-blocks (sub-block allocations ~4-32 KB keyspace) for fast allocation and low-fragment churn; a coalescer thread that merges adjacent micro-blocks into coalesced GPU-resident blocks when aggregate hotness crosses a threshold; and a staged host-residency path that keeps low-affinity coalesced blocks on host with lightweight shadow metadata to enable quick reactivation. Combine this with a tail-swap hysteresis policy to prevent oscillating swap-ins/outs and an async non-blocking reclaim token to rate-limit background compaction.
design_decisions: Micro-block size range: initial default 16KB keyspace; configurable per-model profile
Coalescer runs opportunistically on spare CPU cycles and triggers when host residency ratio > configured threshold
Hotness measure: time-decayed access count + batch-locality score (tokens requested in last N ms)
Tail-swap hysteresis: require sustained hotness > H_up for T_up ms to pull to GPU and sustained coldness < H_down for T_down ms to demote
Host-staged representation uses compressed prefix snapshot + KV pointer map to reduce host memory and network serialization cost
Eviction: prefer demotion (GPU->host) for coalesced blocks rather than immediate discard unless memory pressure is critical
Safety: bounded number of concurrent coalescence jobs to avoid CPU/IO runaway
Observability: expose per-block lifecycle events (alloc, coalesce, promote, demote, evict) for tracing and SLO attribution
implementation_plan: Phase 1: allocator changes to support micro-block allocations and metadata layout; add unit tests for allocation/free semantics
Phase 2: implement coalescer component and in-memory coalesced-block descriptor; add APIs for promotion/demotion
Phase 3: integrate staged host residency path with async serializer and lightweight shadow metadata
Phase 4: implement tail-swap hysteresis and reclaim token rate limiter; add integration tests under synthetic load
Phase 5: benchmarks and canary rollout with per-tenant toggles; iterate on thresholds
Phase 6: documentation, SDK flags, and console metrics wiring

acceptance_criteria: Sustained GPU resident working set reduced by >= 18% on representative multi-tenant trace while matching baseline tail P99 latency within 10%
Number of OOM-triggered fallbacks in controlled stress test reduced to zero for configurations within target budget
No regression in median latency for small request (<256 tokens) workloads
All per-block lifecycle events are emitted and visible in console for canary tenants
Feature gate present and defaults to off for existing tenants; can be enabled per-tenant
test_plan: Unit tests for micro-block alloc/free, fragmentation simulation
Integration tests: coalescer under synthetic skewed-access trace
Load test: continuous batching with mixed short/long sequences across 50 tenants; measure swaps and latency
Fault injection: drop host->gpu promotion and verify graceful degradation
A/B canary: enable for 5% traffic on staging and compare metrics to control group
performance_expectations: Expect 12-25% reduction in GPU memory churn (measured as page-in/page-out events per minute) for skewed token workloads and a 10-20% reduction in end-to-end token cost due to fewer swap-induced recomputations. Tail latency improvements concentrated on P95-P99 for medium-length generations.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind tenant flag and runtime-2.04 coordination
Internal canary on staging with synthetic workloads for 72 hours
Gradual ramp: 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over two weeks with metric gates at each step
Emergency rollback: disable coalescer and force immediate demotion to host for affected tenant
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard: per-tenant GPU resident ratio, coalescer job latency, promotion/demotion counts
Alert: >5x increase in promotion latency over baseline for 5m -> page issue to ENG
SLO: P99 generation latency must not regress by more than 15% in canary during rollout
Audit logs: emit coalescer decisions for postmortem analysis
